learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Africa is too small for them and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Moved US then China then India. Share rose 0 to 31 to 63 to 73 percent, with room left 30.0, 20.6, 11.2 and 8.0 million square kilometres. Each move became disabled; no reset or removal control was visible.
observations.reveal: Corrected to room to spare, gave total 22.0 versus Africa 30.0 million square kilometres and explained Equal Earth versus Mercator distortion. Claimed the countries fit inside Africa.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Three colored labeled outlines lay over blue Africa. Caption explicitly said pieces spill over a coast about 3 percent and totals use area. Reveal inner scroll clipped map top and lower explanation at current position, while area metrics remained visible.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete familiar-country comparison elicits size intuition.
prediction.evidence: Too small selected against fit and exact fill.

interaction.reason: Three meaningful additions update cumulative area but are one-way prescribed steps.
interaction.evidence: Disabled moved countries and no visible reset.

payoff.reason: Area arithmetic and projection explanation are useful, but literal fit wording overstates the admitted coastal spill.
payoff.evidence: Caption about 3 percent spill versus reveal fit inside.

clarity.reason: Labels and totals are clear; packing wording and reveal clipping create friction.
clarity.evidence: Map top clipped and caption qualifies fit.

transfer.reason: Mercator latitude distortion is explained without a new application.
transfer.evidence: US and China stretched more than much of Africa.

accessibility.evidence: Text share and placed-country summary observed; keyboard, screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Three large countries occupy under three quarters of Africa by area.
surprise.evidence: 73 percent with 8.0 million square kilometres left.

visualExplanation.reason: Equal-area overlays expose scale through familiar outlines.
visualExplanation.evidence: US, China and India labeled in distinct colors.

playfulness.evidence: Three move buttons without free placement.

practicalValue.reason: Challenges geographic size judgments from common maps.

depth.reason: Area totals lead into projection distortion.

complexity.reason: Familiar shapes and additive percentages support the comparison.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Separate land area from familiar map appearance and literal packing.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Three sequential buttons; inner scrolling at reveal.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Equal-area projection and Mercator distortion introduced in prose.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Percentages and millions of square kilometres.

whyCool: Recognizable country outlines make a continental area comparison tangible.
caveat: The coastal spill caption conflicts with a literal reading of fit inside; this is an area comparison rather than exact containment.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
